title: Benny Goodman: a 'revolting' personality and the $150 arrangement
summary: Gil says he wrote few arrangements for Goodman, found him unpleasant and recalls an all-night negotiation over fees.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Tell me about working with Pearl Bailey.

When you asked me about Benny Goodman remember, I didn't really work for Benny Goodman much. I wrote just a couple of arrangements for him at certain times. Not, not in his hey day. After all in his hey day he had Jimmy Mundy and Fletcher Henderson, so he was okay. (VOICE FADES OUT).
Later I wrote a couple of things for him. But Benny Goodman is a fairly revolting person.
Oh Really? (LAUGHTER). Now that's what I wanted to know. (LAUGHTER).

You know, he's one of those people that, about the clarinet, he knows the clarinet. Now he was a child prodigy. His first job he worked in knee pants. You know, he played at the Chicago Jazz Group there in knee pants. He's been playing a long time and he really is an artists, a great instrumentalist. But about what makes life work and all

He kept me sitting up there in the Essex House bar one night all night long. He wanted this arrangement from me and he wanted to pay me fifty dollars and said that was the market price. And I said I didn't care what the market price was it was worth one hundred and fifty and I wouldn't do it for a nickel less.

And I sat in that bar, I sat up there all evening and wrangled around with him while he probed me. He'd say, why don't you write for this? I'd say, I don't want to write for...this... Why don't you do this? He was trying to find out whether I was trying to get this extra money out of him, you know, what my circumstances...... Finally, when he realised I really didn't do anything else at all, but that I wanted to get paid for that, then he came through, because you know..........
And he's like Bob Hope, rich, right?
Oh yes, he made a million dollars. But every time, well he was a big hit. He married a rich woman too. He married John Hammond's sister.
( ?). Some family like that. I think it was (Guggenheim?). They have a lot of money. I used to know her well. Alice, I think... ?). So Benny Goodman, from my experience, is nothing much.
